extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/applicants to Canadian federal granting opportunities (SSHRC Insight Grants and Insight Development Grants, CIHR Project Grant, NSERC Discovery Horizons) preparing interdisciplinary project proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting interdisciplinary research applications to the four gateway funding opportunities that may be reviewed by the Tri-Agency Interdisciplinary Peer Review Committee. Covers eligibility, relevance to the interdisciplinary committee, submission routing, timelines, and decision administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding-opportunity eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must meet the eligibility requirements of the funding opportunity (SSHRC Insight Grants and Insight Development Grants, CIHR Project Grant, or NSERC Discovery Horizons) to which they are applying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the specific funding opportunity's eligibility guidance on the relevant granting agency website; this committee is an option only for applications submitted to those gateway competitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-submission requirement (no identical project across agencies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants (or applicant teams) cannot submit an identical project to more than one agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the project is submitted to only one agency/competition; if proposals are materially identical, choose the appropriate gateway funding opportunity and do not duplicate submissions across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible competitions / who may be reviewed by the committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals applying for SSHRC Insight Grants and Insight Development Grants, CIHR Project Grant, and NSERC Discovery Horizons will be eligible to be reviewed by this interdisciplinary peer review committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being eligible for committee review depends on which gateway competition you submit to; consult the listed competitions and their timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition / scope of 'interdisciplinary' for the committee
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purpose of this committee, 'interdisciplinary' is used as an umbrella term to refer inclusively to multidisciplinary, transdisciplinary, and interdisciplinary approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agencies recognize varying usages across disciplines; applicants should treat 'interdisciplinary' broadly when justifying committee relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application relevance to the interdisciplinary committee (breadth across domains)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications considered relevant for review by this committee must represent research across disciplines and subject areas pertaining to two or more of: (1) social sciences and humanities, (2) natural sciences and engineering, and (3) health and wellness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly demonstrate that the proposed work spans at least two of the three domain groups and provide evidence in the application of how multiple disciplinary perspectives are integrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinarity must be central / necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Interdisciplinarity must be a key characteristic of proposed projects, where the project goals could not be achieved without an interdisciplinary approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why disciplinary integration is essential to achieving the research goals, not just additive or multidisciplinary labeling; show how methods, concepts, or theory from multiple fields are needed to deliver outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission routing — choose agency matching dominant discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should submit their application to the gateway funding opportunity that supports the research project’s dominant research discipline or area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the guide 'Selecting the Appropriate Federal Granting Agency' to determine which agency’s mandate aligns best with your proposed research; consult agency webpages for competition-specific requirements and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared-review process / committee composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tri-Agency Interdisciplinary Peer Review Committee will be composed of peer reviewers with broad expertise in interdisciplinary research, recruited in response to the applications submitted and deemed relevant for the committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect reviewers from social sciences, humanities, natural sciences, engineering, and health sciences as needed; applications are pooled across the four gateway funding opportunities for review by this shared committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines and procedural timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Timelines for submission (letters of intent, registrations, full applications), committee meetings, and notices of decision vary by funding opportunity and are set per each competition's schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the specific competition timeline (examples listed: dates for SSHRC Insight Grants, CIHR Project Grant cycles, NSERC Discovery Horizons) and plan application components and internal approvals accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding decisions remain with submitting agency and follow agency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Although reviewed by the Tri-Agency Interdisciplinary Peer Review Committee, funding decisions will be made, funding provided, and grants administered by the agency to which the application was submitted, in accordance with that agency’s guidelines and decision-making processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare to comply with the submitting agency's application format, eligibility checks, reporting, and award administration even when review is conducted by the shared committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation and where to get questions answered
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should consult the relevant granting agency website for competition-specific requirements and timeline; contact information is provided for SSHRC, CIHR, and NSERC for questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use agency support contacts (emails and phone numbers listed) for competition-specific questions; the FAQ and Committee Peer Review Guide provide additional contextual guidance.
